content: Traditional Chinese herbal medicines are commonly utilized in China for the treatment of premenstrual syndrome (PMS). However, their efficacy has not been systematically reviewed to date. The purpose of this study was to assess both the effectiveness and safety of traditional Chinese herbal medicines in managing PMS symptoms. To conduct this review, a comprehensive search was performed across multiple databases, including MEDLINE (from January 1950 to December 2007), EMBASE (from January 1980 to December 2007), the Chinese Biomedical Database (CBM) (from January 1975 to December 2007), the China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) (from January 1994 to December 2007), and the VIP Database (from January 1989 to December 2007). The inclusion criteria were limited to randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that evaluated the efficacy of traditional Chinese herbal medicines for PMS treatment. Two reviewers contacted the original authors of the RCTs to verify the randomization procedures. They also extracted and analyzed data from the trials that met the inclusion criteria. Ultimately, two RCTs involving a total of 549 women were included in the analysis. One of the trials, which was determined to be of higher methodological quality, demonstrated the therapeutic effectiveness of a traditional Chinese herbal medicine known as Jingqianping granule. This study showed statistically significant improvements in symptom relief during the proliferative and premenstrual phases when compared to Xiaoyaowan (Relative Risk [RR] 3.50, 95% Confidence Interval [CI] 1.74 to 7.06). The second trial, which was of lower methodological quality due to a higher risk of bias, reported that women treated with Cipher decoction had a higher recovery rate compared to those taking co-vitamin B6 capsules (RR 48.99, 95% CI 3.06 to 783.99). However, the reliability of this finding is limited due to the study's design flaws. The authors concluded that it is uncommon for claims of efficacy in PMS management to be supported by clinical trials. While one of the included trials was well-designed and provided evidence for the effectiveness of Jingqianping granule in treating PMS, the overall evidence remains insufficient. Further high-quality, well-controlled trials are necessary before definitive conclusions can be drawn regarding the use of traditional Chinese herbal medicines for PMS.
